comparisons.observation: Close view of speaker; no subtitle in the fixed region. Clothing/background produced apparent tokens.
Wide hall view. A preview label appears above the subtitle; correct OCR does not make this featured-speaker text.
Wide hall view with podium and large screen; one visible subtitle line matches OCR.
Seated attendee fills frame. The first subtitle line is read, but the second is replaced by nonsense. Do not treat the attendee as the captioned speaker.
Wide hall and audience; a small speaker label remains above the region but there is no subtitle inside it. OCR outputs background noise.
Close podium-speaker view; one subtitle line matches OCR.
Close podium-speaker view; two subtitle lines match OCR.
Promotional end card has subscription text above the region; the fixed subtitle region contains background graphics, not subtitle words.

limitations: New timestamps with frozen preprocessing, but same upload and assistant; not independent corpus evaluation. All eight images were directly inspected after seeing OCR results. No listening, continuous viewing, word alignment or speaker identification from faces. Region-relative absence does not mean the whole frame contains no text.
decision: Do not scale this fixed-layout OCR as an unattended transcript builder. Separate text-presence detection, transcription correctness and editorial/speaker role. Preserve the failures as development cases; use fresh data to evaluate any revised gate.
confidence_observation: No-subtitle and corrupted-line tokens have lower engine scores here, but no acceptance threshold was predefined. A threshold chosen now would be trained on this evaluation, not independently validated.
